## Why This Is Asked
Demonstrates DR planning for critical control-plane data and ability to perform controlled failover with minimal downtime.

## Key Concepts
- etcd backup/restore; - kubeadm-based control planes; - DR site replication; - cluster health verification; - minimal downtime strategies.

## Code Example
```bash
# Snapshot from healthy member
ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot save /tmp/etcd-snap.db
# Transfer to DR site, then on DR:
etcdctl snapshot restore /tmp/etcd-snap.db --data-dir=/var/lib/etcd
```

- How would you test PITR and verify data consistency?  
- What are caveats with TLS bootstrapping and etcd encryption in transit/rest during DR?

## Why This Is Asked

- Secrets Store CSI driver concept
- Pod rolling restart to refresh mounted secrets

## Why This Is Asked

- NetworkPolicy basics and namespace scoping
- Cross-namespace traffic rules

```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
```

## Why This Is Asked
Real-world issues arise when admission webhooks slow down or fail under load; handling timeouts safely is critical. This question tests debugging workflows, safe remediation strategies, and verification techniques.

## Key Concepts
- MutatingWebhookConfiguration, timeoutSeconds, and failurePolicy settings
- Distinguishing pod creation latency from admission latency
- Observability via kubectl describe, logs, and events

## Code Example
```bash
# Inspect current webhook configuration
kubectl get MutatingWebhookConfiguration <name> -o yaml

# Patch to set failurePolicy to Ignore
kubectl patch MutatingWebhookConfiguration <name> \
  --type='json' \
  -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/webhooks/0/failurePolicy","value":"Ignore"}]'

# Increase timeoutSeconds to 30
kubectl patch MutatingWebhookConfiguration <name> \
  --type='json' \
  -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/webhooks/0/timeoutSeconds","value":30}]'

# Verify webhook pods are healthy
kubectl get pods -n webhook-system -l app=webhook

# Check webhook server logs
kubectl logs -n webhook-system -l app=webhook --tail=100

# Monitor pod creation after fix
kubectl get events -n prod --watch
```

## Why This Is Asked

This tests practical network policy design, scope reduction, and verification in a shared environment, including rollback.

- Pod labeling and namespace scoping
- DNS vs IP-based allowlists in CNI

```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-enricher-api-egress

spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: enricher
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 203.0.113.0/24
```

## Why This Is Asked

```bash
# List all NetworkPolicies in the cluster

# Deploy a debug pod for testing
e kubectl run debug-pod --image=busybox --rm -it --restart=Never -- /bin/sh

# Test connectivity to billing service from debug pod

# Apply minimal egress NetworkPolicy to allow billing service traffic
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-billing-egress
  namespace: <api-namespace>
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: api
  egress:
  - to:
    - pod: {}
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
EOF
```

## Why This Is Asked

```yaml
# SecretProviderClass example (Vault)
apiVersion: secrets-store.csi.x-k8s.io/v1alpha1
kind: SecretProviderClass
metadata:
  name: vault-creds
spec:
  provider: vault
  parameters:
    roleName: "db-role"
    vaultAddress: "https://vault.example.com"
    objects: |
      - objectName: db-credentials
        secretPath: secret/data/db/creds
        secretKey: creds
    refreshInterval: "3600s"
```
